subject: Agriculture
title: Post-War Food Insecurity
description: Learn Post-War Food Insecurity in one minute.

hook.text: After World War II, much of Asia and Africa couldn't feed its growing populations. Hunger was everywhere.

buildup.text: India relied on US food aid—millions of tons of surplus wheat shipped under PL-480 agreements.

discovery.text: Dependence on food imports left nations vulnerable. A delayed shipment meant starvation.

twist.text: President Johnson withheld food shipments to pressure India on policy. Food aid became a political weapon.

climax.text: India's humiliation fueled a national commitment to grow its own food—at any cost. The stage was set.

punchline.text: Hunger drove dependence. Dependence drove revolution.

quiz.question: Why did India's dependence on US food aid become problematic?
options: The US withheld shipments as political leverage
